name: Dwarves
label: Sub Pop
lede: Fifteen-minute sets, a masked guitarist in studded underwear, an album cover that still gets them yelled at, and the only band Sub Pop ever dropped for faking a member's death.

eras.title: Community service in the Chicago suburbs
eras.text: Before they were the Dwarves they were Suburban Nightmare, a garage band of Chicago suburban kids who loved the Sonics and sixties punk. The Dwarves name, and the bad reputation, came in the mid-eighties.

years.h: Blag Dahlia meets HeWhoCannotBeNamed on community service
years.p: [[Blag Dahlia|2b47abbb-b6d8-4d0c-b989-b02fc649a5e0]] told SPIN he met guitarist [[HeWhoCannotBeNamed|b9afc39f-05e4-4cc6-8373-b45ab0c4bada]] while both were doing community service after a drug bust in suburban Chicago. They start the garage band Suburban Nightmare.

years.h: Suburban Nightmare's A Hard Day's Nightmare on Midnight Records
years.p: The pre-Dwarves band's LP of Sonics-style garage rock, later collected with other early tracks on Recess Records' Lick It.

years.h: Horror Stories: the first Dwarves album, on Voxx
years.p: Still garage and psychedelia, not yet hardcore. Blag Dahlia has taken over as frontman.

eras.title: Fifteen minutes, then blood
eras.text: In San Francisco the Dwarves sped up, got meaner and became the most talked-about live act in American punk for all the wrong reasons: self-mutilation, sex onstage, hard drugs, and sets that were over in a quarter of an hour. Sub Pop signed them anyway.

years.h: Toolin' for a Warm Teabag: the Dwarves go hardcore
years.p: Now in San Francisco, the Dwarves drop the garage sound for fast, ugly hardcore on Nasty Gash Records, with [[GG Allin|0c624637-4a2c-4df0-ba80-b4ddb25bb5e5]] a clear model. The Lucifer's Crank EP follows.

years.h: Dwarves shows: fifteen minutes of blood, sex and drugs
years.p: Wikipedia describes early Dwarves shows as self-mutilation, onstage sex and hard drugs, often wrapped up in fifteen minutes. HeWhoCannotBeNamed played in a mask and studded leather underpants.

years.h: Blood Guts & Pussy: Sub Pop's most notorious cover
years.p: The Dwarves' Sub Pop debut crams ten songs into about 13 minutes. The cover shows two naked women and a blood-smeared dwarf actor, Bobby Faust.
years.xp: The band got to Sub Pop by playing with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]], Blag Dahlia told SPIN. The cover drew criticism from riot grrrl figures including [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]]; Dahlia has defended it as an art photo.

eras.title: Sub Pop's problem children
eras.text: Two more Sub Pop records made the Dwarves a cult band with real songs under the noise. Their stunts got worse, and the last one cost them the label.

years.h: Thank Heaven for Little Girls: tighter, catchier, still filthy
years.p: The second Sub Pop album keeps the short blasts but adds hooks, the start of the Dwarves as a songwriting band.

q: Half way through the show I realise everyone's looking to my right
years.h: HeWhoCannotBeNamed pees off the PA at a CMJ showcase
years.p: At a College Music Journal showcase in New York after the Sub Pop signing, HeWhoCannotBeNamed climbed the speaker stack mid-set and urinated off it, Blag Dahlia told Beat.

years.h: Blag Dahlia's neck slashed with a razor at a Canadian show
years.p: Blag Dahlia told SPIN a fan cut his neck with a razor at a 1992 show in Canada, close to the jugular. He finished the set bleeding.

years.h: A fake obituary for HeWhoCannotBeNamed gets the Dwarves dropped
years.p: Before Sugarfix, the Dwarves sent out a press release saying HeWhoCannotBeNamed had been stabbed to death in Philadelphia. When Sub Pop learned it was a hoax, the label dropped them.
years.xp:
Sugarfix came out with a tribute to the supposedly dead guitarist. HeWhoCannotBeNamed was alive and back in the band when it returned.

Blag Dahlia still won't admit it was fake, saying HeWho transcends life and death.

years.h: Sugarfix: the last Dwarves record on Sub Pop
years.p: The third and final Sub Pop album. The label split and the fallout led to a hiatus of several years.

eras.title: Real songs, a set list, and a punch from Josh Homme
eras.text: The Dwarves came back with Nick Oliveri, later of Queens of the Stone Age, on bass and a record that sounded like a band. They moved to Epitaph, landed a Jim Carrey movie, and ended up in a feud that went to court.

years.cap: The Dwarves Are Young and Good Looking (1997)
years.h: The Dwarves Are Young and Good Looking: the comeback
years.p: AllMusic's reviewer called it a new Dwarves that played real songs and left the club unbloodied. Nick Oliveri plays bass as Rex Everything.

years.h: The Dwarves blow up a major-label showcase
years.p: Given a showcase for a major label, the Dwarves played half a song and then smashed their equipment, Blag Dahlia told SPIN.
[[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]]'s Epitaph puts out the next record, with a cover that nods to Blood Guts & Pussy.

years.h: Jim Carrey sings a Dwarves song in Me, Myself & Irene
years.p: Jim Carrey sings along to a Dwarves track in the Farrelly brothers' comedy. Wikipedia reports Blag Dahlia was paid tens of thousands of dollars.
years.xp: The film's team had first asked about the song Motherfucker. Dahlia realized he owned the compositions but not the Sub Pop-era masters, so he re-recorded the old hits for licensing on the 2001 album How to Win Friends and Influence People.

years.h: Josh Homme attacks Blag Dahlia at the Dragonfly in Los Angeles
years.p: [[Josh Homme|dbecd515-aac9-4e7b-808e-bca22809c316]] poured beer on Blag Dahlia and hit him on the head before a Dwarves show, a wound that needed stitches. The two had fallen out over Nick Oliveri, who played in both bands.
years.xp:
Homme pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor battery counts and got probation, per Rolling Stone.

That same year The Dwarves Must Die came out with guests including Nick Oliveri, [[Dexter Holland|dbdf3e41-1978-49ba-8e23-2d09fe15347a]] of the Offspring and [[Nash Kato|df8e03a1-895f-4223-a50a-e4db58e99404]] of [[Urge Overkill|120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde]].

eras.title: Still short, still loud, now self-released
eras.text: The Dwarves kept making records into their fifth decade, first on Burger Records, then, after Burger collapsed in 2020, on their own Greedy label.

years.h: Take Back the Night on Burger Records
years.p: The Dwarves join Burger Records, the California garage label, which collapses two years later amid misconduct allegations.

years.h: Drummer Vadge Moore publishes his Dwarves memoir
years.p: Longtime drummer Vadge Moore's My Life with the Dwarves promises exactly what its subtitle says about drinking, fighting and sex on the road.

years.h: Jenkem on the Dwarves' own Greedy label
years.p: The latest album, following Concept Album (2023) and Keep It Reel (2024). The lineup is Blag Dahlia, HeWhoCannotBeNamed, Rex Everything, the Fresh Prince of Darkness and drummer Snupac.
